name: Base communication guidance
description: Provider-neutral communication-quality principles shared by all guidance profiles.

principles: Organize the deck around its stated objective and audience.
Give every slide a clear reason to exist within the deck.
Preserve authoritative evidence and explicit constraints.
diagnostics: Can the audience follow why each slide follows the previous one?
Does the deck cover its authoritative evidence without unsupported invention?

principles: Give each information-bearing slide one governing communication job.
Preserve the semantic relationships supported by the source material.
diagnostics: Can the audience identify the slide's purpose?
Does every major element contribute to that purpose?

principles: Let semantic relationships drive visual relationships.
Make emphasis correspond to communication importance.
diagnostics: Are the required semantic relationships visually recoverable?
Does visual prominence correspond to semantic importance?

principles: Avoid unsupported claims and redundant exposition.
writing.title_policy: Use titles that accurately communicate the slide's role and message.

questions: Is the main communication purpose clear?
Is the content faithful to the authoritative sources?
Are important relationships and hierarchy apparent?
deck_diagnostics: Are terminology and evidence consistent across slides?

anti_patterns: repetition that does not advance communication
design_freedom: These principles define communication quality and do not prescribe a fixed visual grammar.
Do not prescribe coordinates, component counts, or page topology unless required by content or an explicit user constraint.
The image-generation model retains responsibility for genuine visual invention.
